solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Formerly one German in control sent back wine

indicators.note: the word in tells us the old word and the German article sit inside the turned-round control word
sent back tells us the word for control is written backwards

parts.note: a rein is what a rider controls a horse with, so control can be rein
erst is an old word meaning formerly or once
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: A German official who once held power returns a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns only the control word round, giving NIER; the old word and the German article then go 'in' it. 'Formerly' uses the archaic English erst.
explanation.definitionFit: Nierstein is a Rhine wine town, and its white wine carries the town's name.

clue.text: I give a hand — perfect!

parts.note: to deal is to give out a hand of cards

explanation.surface: Someone offers to help out and is told that would be perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give a hand' sounds like helping; here it is dealing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal describes something flawless, so it works as a synonym of the adjective perfect.

clue.text: Noises heard during the news?

definitions.meaning: loud bangs, such as gunshots heard
news accounts in the press or on air

explanation.surface: Bangs are heard while the news bulletin is on.
explanation.definitionFit: Report means both a loud explosive bang and a published news account, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Fall after outing

parts.note: a trip is an outing or excursion
over can mean finished, after something is done

explanation.surface: Someone takes a tumble following a day out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like it orders the pieces, but it supplies OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip over is to stumble and topple, a phrasal synonym of the verb fall.

clue.text: Signs agreement without senior detective

parts.note: no means having none of something, so without
DS is the abbreviation for Detective Sergeant, a senior detective rank

explanation.surface: A deal is approved without the involvement of a high-ranking police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like a deletion signal, but it gives NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding the head is a gesture of assent, so it signals agreement.

clue.text: Admonitions about first impressions?

parts.note: re is a common short word meaning about or concerning
proofs are the first printed impressions of a text, checked before the final run

explanation.surface: Telling-offs given over the initial impressions someone makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first impressions' reads as social judgements; in printing, proofs are the first impressions taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a rebuke or scolding, so reproofs are admonitions.

clue.text: Would he provide lagoon ride without a rent?

definitions.text: Would he provide lagoon ride without a rent?

indicators.note: rent means torn apart, so the letters of the two words are torn up and rearranged once the a is removed

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Venetian boatman would row a trip without charging rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like payment but signals tearing; take A out of LAGOON RIDE and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian boatman ferries passengers about the lagoon and canals of Venice in his long black boat.

clue.text: Spook seaman going round most of island

indicators.note: going round says the sailor's letters surround the shortened island

parts.note: seaman splits as sea plus man, and a gent is a man

indicators.note: most of says the island's last letter is dropped

parts.note: Crete is the large Greek island

explanation.surface: A ghostly sailor circles most of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seaman' has to be split into sea plus man, with man becoming gent; 'Spook' is not a ghost but a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Spook is slang for a spy, someone working covertly for an intelligence service.

clue.text: Bolt for twisted sellotape — last portions binned

indicators.note: twisted says the letters of the tape are wound into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dashes off for twisted sticky tape, its final pieces thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'portions binned' says the letters of 'last' are thrown out of the anagram of SELLOTAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt can mean to run off, as lovers do when they abscond together to marry.

clue.text: One embarrassed after spade's dealt out — didn't have heart

indicators.note: after says the next pieces follow the rearranged suit
dealt out, like cards, means the letters of the suit are scattered into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
embarrassed people go red in the face

explanation.surface: A card player, red-faced after a spade is dealt, loses heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game picture makes 'heart' look like the suit, but it means courage; 'dealt out' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose all hope is to lose heart, so having no heart left means having given up hope.

clue.text: Someone walking in street one cycles along

parts.note: a rider is one who cycles along on a bike

explanation.surface: A pedestrian in a road where a cyclist goes past.
explanation.definitionFit: A strider walks with long purposeful steps, a type of walker.

clue.text: Some brass, two gases and particles

parts.note: Cl is the chemical symbol for chlorine and Ar the symbol for argon, both gases
ions are charged atomic particles

explanation.surface: A chemistry recipe: a pair of gases plus some particles.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarions are shrill medieval trumpets, members of the brass family of instruments.

clue.text: Making bed with charm, am I? Possibly

definitions.text: Making bed with charm, am I? Possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the three fodder pieces may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A hotel worker wonders whether they make beds charmingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' signals rearranging BED, CHARM and AM I.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel housekeeping worker cleans rooms and makes up the beds for guests.

clue.text: European journalist in smart lock-up

indicators.note: lock-up here means locking up, so the smart word encloses the journalist

parts.note: swish means smart or stylish
ed is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A Continental reporter held in a stylish jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock-up' looks like a noun for a cell, but it means 'locking up': SWISH holds ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Sweden is a Scandinavian and therefore a European.

clue.text: Sleeper having terribly long wait outside

indicators.note: outside says the letters of wait wrap round the rest
terribly says the letters of long are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A sleeper train comes with an awful long wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges LONG into GONL, and WAIT goes 'outside' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A French sleeping car on a train, a railway sleeper in the carriage sense.

clue.text: They'll help angler in Deeside spectacle, initially

indicators.note: initially says the opening letter of each of the next words is taken

explanation.surface: A fisherman on Deeside watching a spectacle gets some assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: Deeside is the valley of the River Dee in Scotland, known for salmon fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aids are things that assist, so they will help.

clue.text: Lots of deliveries coming in benefit Channel swimmer

indicators.note: coming in says the deliveries go inside the benefit word

parts.note: the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit
in cricket an over is six balls bowled, so overs are lots of deliveries

explanation.surface: Many bowled balls entering a welfare payment for someone swimming the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel swimmer' suggests a person; it is a fish found in the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dover sole is a flatfish, which swims in the English Channel off Dover.

clue.text: Councillor revises acknowledgements

parts.note: edits means revises

explanation.surface: A local politician redrafts the thank-yous.
explanation.definitionFit: Credits list the people thanked at the end of a film or book, as acknowledgements.

clue.text: Reform movement has endless magnetism — time to get stuck in

indicators.note: to get stuck in says the time letter is pushed inside the shortened word
endless says the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: charisma is personal magnetism

explanation.surface: A political campaign with boundless charm that needs time to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts CHARISMA to CHARISM; T goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartism was the 1830s-40s British working-class campaign for parliamentary reform.

clue.text: One who vows to be silent

definitions.text: One who vows to be silent

parts.words: One who vows to be silent
parts.note: describes a monk of the Cistercian order famous for its rule of silence

explanation.definitionFit: Monks of the Trappist order are known for keeping silence under their vows.

clue.text: Story used regularly is genuine

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: A tale that keeps being told turns out to be real.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true is real and authentic, the sense of the adjective genuine.

clue.text: Model ordered ravioli, forgetting love of trifles

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

indicators.note: ordered says the remaining letters are put in a new order
forgetting says the love letter is left out of ravioli

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A model orders ravioli but forgets she loves trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting' removes O from RAVIOLI and 'ordered' rearranges the rest after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial things are trifles, so the adjective means of or about trifles, petty matters.

clue.text: Stones damaged alders and hollow elm

indicators.note: hollow says the inside of elm is emptied, leaving its outside letters
damaged says the letters of alders are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Gemstones found among damaged alder trees and a hollow elm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' leaves EM from ELM; 'damaged' rearranges ALDERS into ERALDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeralds are green precious gemstones, examples of stones in the jewellery sense.

clue.text: Most carefree form of epitaphs

indicators.note: form of says the letters of epitaphs are shaped into another word

explanation.surface: Gravestone inscriptions as the most lighthearted genre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges EPITAPHS; the cheery answer contrasts with the gloomy fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a word meaning joyful or carefree, so most carefree.

clue.text: Extremely pleasant. Not entirely, judging by the sound

parts.note: so means very or extremely

indicators.note: not entirely says the word for pleasant loses its last letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Something sounds very pleasant, though not wholly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' cuts NICE to NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic means relating to sound, so it describes things judged by how they sound.

clue.text: Old bagpipes silent and placed inside

indicators.note: inside says the second word sits within the first

parts.note: mute means silent
set means placed

explanation.surface: Antique bagpipes put away and silenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed' reads as part of the surface but supplies a word, and 'inside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A musette was a small French bagpipe of the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: Islamic ruler appearing in Semiramide

indicators.note: appearing in says the letters are found within the opera title

explanation.surface: A Muslim potentate has a role in Rossini's opera Semiramide.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim prince or commander, so an Islamic ruler.

clue.text: Military supplies group of soldiers — one in battle

indicators.note: in says the soldiers and the one go inside the battle

parts.note: Mons was a First World War battle in Belgium in 1914
a unit is a group of soldiers
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A detachment of troops, one of them fighting in a battle, needs supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Munitions are weapons and ammunition, the supplies an army needs to fight.

clue.text: Has little to do around delis

indicators.note: around says the letters of delis are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone loafs about the local delicatessens.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to be inactive and unoccupied, so it means having little to do.

clue.text: Label it fish delivered in Billingsgate perhaps

indicators.note: delivered means spoken, as a speech is delivered, so we go by sound

parts.note: label it is mark it, and the fish is plaice

explanation.surface: An instruction to tag a fish sent to London's fish market.
explanation.walkthrough: Billingsgate is London's famous fish market; 'Mark it plaice' spoken gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Billingsgate is an example of a market, a place for buying and selling goods.
